fields.topology_type: Tree-shaped 'hierarchy' rooted at a Root Complex (RC). Below the RC: optional Switches that aggregate multiple Endpoints, plus optional PCI Express-to-PCI/PCI-X Bridges. Every PCIe Link is point-to-point and dual-simplex; there is no shared-medium 'bus' anywhere in the fabric. Optional Cross-Link interconnect (Advanced Peer-to-Peer Communication) allows two separate hierarchies to interoperate.

supported_topologies.name: Single RC + single Endpoint
supported_topologies.description: Simplest case: one Link between RC and one Endpoint.

supported_topologies.name: RC + Switch + N Endpoints
supported_topologies.description: Switch upstream port connects to RC; downstream ports each connect to one Endpoint.

supported_topologies.name: Cascaded Switches
supported_topologies.description: Multi-level tree; each Switch hides its Endpoints behind virtual PCI-to-PCI bridges.

supported_topologies.name: RC + PCI Express-to-PCI/PCI-X Bridge
supported_topologies.description: Allows legacy parallel-PCI / PCI-X devices to attach to a PCIe RC.

supported_topologies.name: Advanced Peer-to-Peer (Cross-Link)
supported_topologies.description: Optional. Two RCs / hierarchies connect via Cross-Link Switches; details in a separate Advanced PCI Express Packet Switching Specification.

master_slave_role_summary.description: Top of one hierarchy; connects CPU/memory to PCIe fabric; must generate Configuration Requests as Requester; may generate I/O Requests; must not support Lock semantics as Completer.

Logical assembly of virtual PCI-to-PCI bridges; forwards TLPs unmodified; must not split a TLP into smaller TLPs; arbitrates between ingress ports on per-VC basis (round-robin or weighted round-robin).
Type 0 Configuration Space header; must support Configuration Requests as Completer; must NOT generate I/O Requests; must NOT support Lock semantics.
Type 0 header; may support I/O space + Lock semantics for legacy software compatibility; must not issue Locked Requests.
One PCIe Port + one or more PCI/PCI-X bus interfaces; supports Lock semantics from PCIe→PCI direction (for deadlock prevention).

fields.interconnect_role: PCI Express is a tree of point-to-point Links. There is no protocol-layer router; Switches act as fan-out and address-based forwarders, but they cannot drop, split, or reorder TLPs (except within ordering rules). Each PCIe Link is independent — TLP delivery is guaranteed at the Link layer by ACK/NAK + replay, and at the end-to-end layer optionally by ECRC.

ordering_guarantees.producer_consumer: PCI / PCI-X compliant producer-consumer ordering model preserved end-to-end through Switches.
ordering_guarantees.relaxed_ordering_optin: TLPs may set the Relaxed Ordering attribute to opt out of certain strict ordering rules for performance.
ordering_guarantees.virtual_channel_isolation: Traffic on different VCs has no ordering relationship to traffic on other VCs; this enables traffic-class differentiation and prevents head-of-line blocking.
ordering_guarantees.completion_ordering: Completions returned to a Requester are NOT ordered against new Requests, allowing pipelining; ordering within a sequence of split-Completion fragments IS preserved.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: PCI Express defines four address spaces: Memory, I/O, Configuration, Message. Memory space is the primary data path (DMA + memory-mapped registers). I/O space is legacy (Legacy Endpoints only). Configuration space is the per-device control plane (256 B + 4 KB extended). Message space replaces sideband signals (INTx, PME, error, vendor-defined).

device_classification.root_complex: Connects CPU + memory to PCIe; one per hierarchy.
device_classification.switch: Aggregates N downstream ports into one upstream port; appears as multiple virtual PCI-to-PCI bridges.
device_classification.pci_express_endpoint: Modern Endpoint; no I/O space; no Lock semantics.
device_classification.legacy_endpoint: PCI-compatible Endpoint; may use I/O space + Lock.
